incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to the Quanum Lab Services Manager (LSM) ordering and results platform.
incidents.impact: Quest took the system offline and warned that some patient data may have been accessed; no group has claimed credit and the company says the incident is unrelated to the PHP2Shell flaws.

incidents.vector: Breach of a peripheral digital service or data-handling system rather than SBI's core banking platform.
incidents.impact: An actor using the handle "Siriusim" posted roughly 3,897 customer records on BreachForums, including KYC documents, loan files, and PII, feeding India's underground data-resale market.

incidents.vector: A flaw in eMudhra's April 2025 key-generation ceremony produced intermediate CA private keys with only 3-8 bits of entropy instead of 384, making them trivially recoverable.
incidents.impact: Eight intermediate CA certificates (six TLS, two code-signing) were compromised, allowing potential server impersonation and traffic interception; browsers revoked trust and eMudhra is exiting the CA business entirely.

incidents.victim: European government entity; organizations worldwide running vulnerable PHP
incidents.vector: Unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP core (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619, "PHP2Shell") exploited via an agentic AI attack platform.
incidents.impact: At one European government target, an agentic attacker harvested password hashes and MFA secrets and attempted Domain Admin escalation within two hours of exploitation; banks, airlines, and governments worldwide took sites offline as a precaution, with millions of internet-facing PHP services still exposed.

incidents.victim: LiteLLM (BerriAI) users — developer, CI/CD, and cloud environments
incidents.vector: Stolen GitHub developer credentials were used to redirect LiteLLM's release workflow to a lookalike repository, publishing a malicious PyPI/Docker release (v1.107.0) that ran a credential-stealing payload automatically via Python startup hooks.
incidents.impact: The payload harvested developer, cloud, browser, and AI-provider credentials across any environment that started Python with the package installed, not just active LiteLLM deployments; this is LiteLLM's second supply-chain compromise this year.

incidents.victim: ccTLD registries for American Samoa (.as), Ghana (.gh), and Sierra Leone (.sl)
incidents.vector: Modification of DNS records to pass domain-ownership verification checks and obtain fraudulent HTTPS certificates for specific domains.
incidents.impact: The hijack enabled impersonation of Google and other organizations' services at the registry level, a more severe compromise than a typical single-domain hijack.

incidents.vector: Breach of the cloud hosting provider leading to theft of customers' encrypted environment variables.
incidents.impact: Attackers likely decrypted some variables to obtain API keys and other credentials; Railway believes the incident is part of a broader wave of attacks targeting AI providers and notified affected providers to revoke exposed keys.

incidents.vector: Unspecified breach of South Korean retail chain systems.
incidents.impact: Data on roughly 2.76 million customers was stolen.

incidents.vector: Unspecified breach affecting the game publisher's customer systems.
incidents.impact: Personal data of more than 11.7 million Capcom gamers was stolen, mostly usernames, emails, and account technical details.

incidents.vector: A hacker breached the Japanese VPS provider and installed malware on more than 26,700 Desktop Cloud servers seeking to steal trading and securities credentials.
incidents.impact: Onamae shut down all affected servers within a day of detecting the breach.

incidents.vector: Breach of the Japanese brokerage's Tradeworks internet trading system.
incidents.impact: Data belonging to nearly 5,000 traders was accessed and unauthorized purchase orders were placed on at least seven accounts, which the firm described as the attackers testing their access.

incidents.victim: Organizations across education, financial services, healthcare, government, manufacturing, and other sectors running unpatched PAN-OS GlobalProtect
incidents.vector: Exploitation of PAN-OS authentication-bypass flaw CVE-2026-0257 to establish VPN sessions, bypass MFA, and pivot to vCenter/ESXi hypervisors for offline credential dumping against domain controllers.
incidents.impact: Ransomware operators have been exploiting this flaw since June 2026 across numerous industries, deploying ransomware after harvesting domain-wide credentials; an update this week confirmed continued active exploitation on unpatched devices.

incidents.victim: CyberLogitec and 40+ downstream port authorities, maritime, and shipping companies
incidents.vector: Supply chain compromise of CyberLogitec, a South Korean maritime IT services provider, used to pivot into 40+ downstream customer networks.
incidents.impact: The n0n ransomware and extortion group listed victims spanning 18 countries and demanded a combined $1.2 billion in ransoms; most refused to pay and had data leaked, making this the largest maritime-sector cyberattack since NotPetya in 2016.

incidents.victim: FBI (via contractor Accenture — Oracle PeopleSoft platform)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of an unpatched Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability at contractor Accenture, which failed to install available security patches.
incidents.impact: ShinyHunters stole personal and business data belonging to nearly all FBI special agents and threatened publication; the FBI dropped Accenture as a contractor, and the ensuing investigation led to multiple arrests, including ransomware negotiators accused of colluding with the extortion group and a murder-for-hire plot allegation.

incidents.victim: Government agency device users (via ad impressions on government networks)
incidents.vector: Zero-click mercenary spyware delivered through targeted online advertising served by the ad network Discover-Tech, which held "certified" status with major ad exchanges.
incidents.impact: A Citizen Lab/Confiant report ('AdFection') found spyware-serving ads received impressions on U.S. government networks; Google and several ad networks have banned Discover-Tech, but other vendors have not responded.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of FortiManager flaw CVE-2024-47575 for initial access, followed by CVE-2025-61624 privilege escalation to deploy the memory-resident PEERSTITCH implant on FortiOS daemons.
incidents.impact: Attackers exfiltrated configuration, credential, and cryptographic material for more than 500 managed FortiGate firewalls and used stolen credentials to intercept traffic; exposure was confirmed within the provider's own environment, not its clients' networks.

incidents.vector: Breach of TiDB Cloud backend systems by the FulcrumSec hacking group.
incidents.impact: Attackers had access between September 9 and October 7, reportedly reaching CRM customer data, JIRA tickets, source code, and service analytics.

incidents.vector: A threat actor compromised more than 330 Tor relays, infected them with Ebury Linux malware, and converted them into exit relays.
incidents.impact: The compromised exit relays intercepted SSH connections and downgraded email connections to steal unencrypted traffic for three days before a researcher detected and reported the campaign.

incidents.victim: 27 compromised e-commerce retailers (105 targeted), including at least one Fortune 500 company
incidents.vector: A single attacker used autonomous agentic AI hacking systems (including Hermes, Strix, and Cairn) to scan and exploit 105 e-commerce sites over five days.
incidents.impact: At least 600,000 payment card records were stolen from two companies, credit-card skimmers were installed on five sites, and the rest saw some degree of illicit access, at an average cost of about $25 per compromised target.
